title: POC Premortem: Harness Benchmark Scope & Failover Plan
summary: Kickoff premortem for the POC benchmark harness: agree success criteria, decide streaming vs non-streaming approach, define load profiles and fallbacks, and assign deliverables for a heavy-run the week of 2027-06-28.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-21 16:00 PT, duration ~62m. Attendees: Maya, Jonas (Redwood); Priya, Carlos, Evelyn (Aurelia).

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time, um this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Jonas, our systems SE is here. Could we go around real quick?
[00:07] Priya Menon: Hi Maya, Priya here. Head of ML at Aurelia. We run a retrieval-augmented summarization product, latency is like... delicate for us.
[00:13] Carlos Diaz: Carlos, platform. I'll be shipping the scripts to you and running the harness on our side.
[00:18] Jonas Mercer: Great, hi all. My plan today is to surface the failure modes and make sure our benchmark harness covers them — streaming fallthrough, kv cache warmup, coldstarts.
[00:26] Evelyn Shaw: Evelyn, SRE. I'm mostly concerned with on-call surface and graceful degradation.
[00:31] Maya: Perfect. High level: you gave us perf targets in the RFP doc but let's sanity check. Priya, what's non-negotiable?
[00:40] Priya: For user-perceived latency we need 95th < 450ms for short queries (avg tokens ~60). Throughput target is 120 reqs/s steady state for the pilot. If we can't hit both, we'll accept increased cost but not increased p95.
[00:52] Jonas: Okay 450ms p95 with 60 tokens. We should define whether that's with streaming enabled or non-streaming end-to-end. Streaming lowers TTF-first-token but can increase server-side overhead depending on batching.
[01:05] Carlos: Our app currently does streaming client-side for partial results. We prefer streaming but can fall back. Important: our client scripts include re-entrancy and token-level post-processing, which the harness needs to run.
[01:18] Maya: Good — so delivering a harness run that mirrors your client scripts is key. Carlos can you share the scripts and a small sample dataset (1000 queries) and also a tokenization note?
[01:28] Carlos: Yes, I'll upload to the share today: s3://aurelia-shared/poctools/scripts.zip. Note: we use a BPE variant that splits on underscores; sometimes token counts differ from HF counts.
[01:38] Jonas: That's important for throughput modeling — token mismatch can change batching behavior. We'll add a tokenization adapter in the harness.
[01:44] Priya: Also we have a warm cache scenario where 70% of requests hit cached prefix, and a cold start scenario where cache empty. We want both tested.
[01:52] Jonas: We'll model that with two traffic slices: warm (70% prefix reuse) and cold (no reuse), plus a blended ramp. We'll also include a KV-cache warmup script that primes top-20 prefixes.
[02:04] Evelyn: On failure modes: if a model variant is out of capacity, can Redwood fallback to smaller quantized variant? We need deterministic fallback to avoid 5xx spikes.
[02:12] Jonas: Yes, we can route to a lower-capacity quantized variant automatically. We'll instrument the harness to trigger that by simulating capacity limits and measuring latency/cost delta.
[02:21] Maya: Let's call that the 'fallthrough policy' in the runbook. We'll document thresholds — e.g., if queue latency > 100ms for 30s, switch model.
[02:29] Priya: Sounds fine. But we also need to know accuracy impact. Can you snapshot a small eval set to measure regen quality between full and quantized models?
[02:37] Jonas: Absolutely. Put a 200-example eval set in the same share, we'll run a quality delta job post-benchmark.
[02:44] Carlos: On streaming vs non-streaming: when you stream, we sometimes abort after first chunk, which affects throughput accounting. How will harness treat aborted streams?
[02:53] Jonas: Harness will replicate your client abort pattern if you annotate scripts. By default aborted requests count as completed for throughput and will log partial tokens and final status. We can parameterize abort probability per profile.
[03:04] Maya: We should also align on telemetry — what headers/metrics you want back. Evelyn, what do you need?
[03:11] Evelyn: Trace id propagation, per-request token count, total latency, model variant, and a boolean 'from_cache'. Also we'll want histogram buckets for tail latency.
[03:21] Jonas: We'll expose prometheus-style metrics and a per-request JSON line in object storage. We'll provide a manifest of metric names so you can wire into your dashboards.
[03:29] Priya: Timeline question: we want a heavy-run next week to validate SLA. Is that realistic?
[03:35] Maya: Yes, if we get scripts and sample data by end-of-day tomorrow we can prepare harness adapters and run a first pass on Wednesday. Heavy-run week of 6/28 is doable.
[03:45] Carlos: Dependencies: we need a limited test account for Redwood Dedicated endpoints or hosted API creds. Also KMS access notes — we use a customer-managed key in prod. For the pilot, we can use ephemeral keys.
[03:56] Jonas: For telemetry and secret handling we'll use short-lived creds. If you want VPC/private deployment runs, that adds a 2-week setup for private connectors — separate from this POC.
[04:06] Priya: For acceptance, aside from p95 <450ms and 120rps, we'll require no more than 0.5% 5xx and quality delta < 2% on rouge or F1 depending on task.
[04:17] Maya: Noted. We'll capture quality delta and error rates in the final report.
[04:21] Carlos: A small note: token counting differences caused us trouble in earlier benchmarks with other vendors; please include raw tokenization logs so we can reconcile.
[04:30] Jonas: We'll dump tokenization logs and a mapping for 1k sample queries so you can cross-check.
[04:34] Priya: How about cost estimates? We need an apples-to-apples for streaming and non-streaming runs.
[04:40] Maya: Jonas will produce a cost/lantency estimate: per-1k tokens cost and p95 for streaming vs non-streaming. We'll include model quantization options.
[04:48] Jonas: For the heavy run we'll also capture per-token GPU utilization and batch sizes so you can see where unit economics come from.
[04:55] Evelyn: On runbook and on-call: if the heavy-run trips a circuit, who will handle mitigation? We want a playbook.
[05:01] Maya: Redwood will own run engineering for the run window; we'll provide a runbook PDF and a slack channel. Post-run handoff to Aurelia on-call for production is part of the deliverable.
[05:11] Priya: Cool. Anything about network topology? We want regional affinity to reduce RTT. We'll prefer us-west on both sides.
[05:18] Jonas: We'll pin the run to us-west and capture RTT samples. If needed we can add an edge proxy to reduce hops.
[05:25] Maya: Let's recap next steps and action items.
[05:29] Priya: Quick question — competitor stuff: we tested with OpenAI and Vertex on a quick run and saw better tail with Redwood in earlier decks, can you include that comparison in the report?
[05:39] Maya: We can include a high-level competitor bench but won't surface exact infra. We'll provide comparative p95 and cost-per-1k tokens.
[05:45] Carlos: I'll upload scripts and tokenization notes today and share the S3 link in the CRM thread.
[05:50] Jonas: I'll prepare the KV-cache warmup script and coldstart script and a harness adapter for your tokenization. I'll also add the fallthrough policy test harness.
[05:58] Maya: I'll send the benchmark template and the run schedule. We'll confirm the heavy run for 2027-06-29 02:00 UTC (week of 6/28).
[06:06] Evelyn: I'll be on the run and will monitor and escalate if needed.
[06:10] Priya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription errors — e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"; "quantized" sometimes "quantity (quantiz)".
